title: Stalk of a tensor product of modules on a ringed space
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], let $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$ be sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $x\in X$. There is a canonical isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules $$(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)_x\;\xrightarrow{\sim}\;\mathcal F_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal G_x,$$ natural in $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$.

proof.text: *Setting and stalks.* Let $x\in X$. The open neighbourhoods of $x$, ordered by reverse inclusion, form a directed set $I_x$. For every presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal P$ on $X$ the stalk $\mathcal P_x=\varinjlim_{U\in I_x}\mathcal P(U)$ is an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module with $r_x\,s_x=(rs)_x$ for $r\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, $s\in\mathcal P(U)$; every element of $\mathcal P_x$ is a germ, and a morphism $\varphi$ of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules induces the $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear map $\varphi_x:s_x\mapsto\varphi(s)_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. This applies to $\mathcal F$, $\mathcal G$, $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G$ and to the presheaf tensor product $\mathcal P=\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G$, $\mathcal P(U)=\mathcal F(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\mathcal G(U)$, whose restriction maps are $s\otimes t\mapsto s|_V\otimes t|_V$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

*Sheafification does not change the stalk.* Let $\theta:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P^\#=\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G$ be the sheafification map [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] the underlying sheaf of abelian groups of the sheafification of the presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal P$ is the sheafification of $\mathcal P$ as a presheaf of abelian groups, with $\theta$ as its unit, and $\theta$ is $\mathcal O_X$-linear. By [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-sheafification-space] (on the topological space $X$) the induced map $\theta_x:\mathcal P_x\to(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)_x$, $p_x\mapsto\theta_U(p)_x$, is an isomorphism of abelian groups. It is $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear: given $a\in\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $\xi\in\mathcal P_x$, write (shrinking to a common neighbourhood, $I_x$ being directed) $a=r_x$, $\xi=p_x$ with $r\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, $p\in\mathcal P(U)$; then $\theta_x(a\xi)=\theta_x((rp)_x)=\theta_U(rp)_x=(r\,\theta_U(p))_x=r_x\,\theta_U(p)_x=a\,\theta_x(\xi)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. So $\theta_x$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 008B (lemma-stalk-tensor-sheaf-modules), proof: 'Follows directly from Lemma 007K and the fact that taking stalks commutes with sheafification'

proof.text: *The stalk of the presheaf tensor product.* By definition $\mathcal P_x=\varinjlim_{U\in I_x}\mathcal F(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\mathcal G(U)$ with transition maps $s\otimes t\mapsto s|_V\otimes t|_V$ (step 1). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-tensor-varying-rings] to the directed set $I_x$ and the systems $A_U=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $M_U=\mathcal F(U)$, $N_U=\mathcal G(U)$ with the restriction maps (commutative rings, and semilinear restrictions since $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ are $\mathcal O_X$-modules): here $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $M=\mathcal F_x$, $N=\mathcal G_x$, the coprojections are the germ maps, the $A$-module structures of the lemma ($r_x\,s_x=(rs)_x$) are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], and $T=\mathcal P_x$ with its $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module structure. The lemma gives an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules $\psi:\mathcal P_x\to\mathcal F_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal G_x$ with $\psi((s\otimes t)_x)=s_x\otimes t_x$ for $s\in\mathcal F(U)$, $t\in\mathcal G(U)$, $x\in U$. This is Sheaves, Lemma 007K for the presheaf tensor product.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 007K (lemma-stalk-tensor-presheaf-modules, proof omitted: written out here)

proof.text: *The isomorphism and the germs of $s\otimes t$.* Put $\Phi=\psi\circ\theta_x^{-1}:(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)_x\to\mathcal F_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal G_x$, an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules by steps 2 and 3. For an open $U\ni x$, $s\in\mathcal F(U)$, $t\in\mathcal G(U)$, the section $s\otimes t\in(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)(U)$ of the statement is $\theta_U(s\otimes t)$, so its germ is $\theta_U(s\otimes t)_x=\theta_x((s\otimes t)_x)$ and $\Phi((s\otimes t)_x)=\psi((s\otimes t)_x)=s_x\otimes t_x$. Moreover the germs $(s\otimes t)_x$ generate $(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)_x$ as an abelian group: every element is $\theta_x(p_x)$ for some $p=\sum_k s_k\otimes t_k\in\mathcal P(U)$, hence equals $\sum_k(s_k\otimes t_k)_x$.

*Naturality.* Let $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ and $\gamma:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ be morphisms of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. The morphism $\varphi\otimes\gamma:\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G\to\mathcal F'\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G'$ is the image under the sheafification functor of the morphism of presheaves $\mathcal P\to\mathcal P'$, $s\otimes t\mapsto\varphi(s)\otimes\gamma(t)$, i.e. the unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear map with $(\varphi\otimes\gamma)\circ\theta=\theta'\circ(\varphi\otimes_p\gamma)$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; hence $(\varphi\otimes\gamma)(s\otimes t)=\varphi(s)\otimes\gamma(t)$ for sections $s,t$ over $U$. The two additive maps $\Phi'\circ(\varphi\otimes\gamma)_x$ and $(\varphi_x\otimes\gamma_x)\circ\Phi$ from $(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)_x$ to $\mathcal F'_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal G'_x$ both send $(s\otimes t)_x$ to $\varphi(s)_x\otimes\gamma(t)_x$ (step 4 and [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]: $\varphi_x(s_x)=\varphi(s)_x$), and these germs generate (step 4), so the maps are equal: $\Phi$ is natural in $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$.
